sections_detected: Budget-Constrained Combinatorial Optimization and Project Portfolio Selection
Power Grid Investment Planning and Project Review Decision Methods
Relation to TRACE-MOEA and Gap Statement
Budget-Constrained Portfolio Review as Multi-Objective Selection
Ablation Study: Scenario-Dependent Forward Effects and Unresolved Substitution
Historical Outcome Consistency: MISO MTEP16 Backtest

primary_story: BiLo-NSGA augments NSGA-II with budget-aware project-vocabulary local moves and move logging on a public proxy benchmark, yielding a modest hypervolume gain whose resolved component evidence is limited to scenario-dependent forward insertion.
primary_result: Across eight proxy scenarios with 30 runs per stochastic method, BiLo-NSGA reports pooled hypervolume 0.17190 versus 0.17000 for NSGA-II, a 1.12% gain obtained with additional local evaluations and 2.74 times the measured runtime; forward insertion resolves positively in three scenarios, whereas atomic substitution has no demonstrated accuracy benefit.
positive_findings: The manuscript consistently retains the unfavorable and null component results in the abstract, results, discussion, and conclusion rather than converting them into a superiority claim.

Deterministic baselines are treated descriptively rather than as 30 independent observations, and the primary stochastic tests state their correction family, effect measure, and confidence-interval convention.
A direct add/delete/swap Pareto-local-search control and separate no-forward, no-backward, and legacy-deletion controls materially improve the evidential coverage.
The manuscript clearly separates trace production from explanation quality and bounds both external backtests as descriptive consistency checks.
Limitations concerning proxy attributes, synthetic costs, outcome imbalance, construct overlap, portfolio dependence, one benchmark family, and absent load-flow validation are unusually explicit.
The intended beneficiaries—utility planning departments and investment review boards—are identified, while operational effectiveness is not claimed as established.

issues.location: Sections 4 and 5.2; Sections 6.1, 6.6, and 6.7; Tables 3, 4, and 7
issues.manuscript_evidence: All evolutionary methods receive 40 individuals for 40 generations, but BiLo-NSGA additionally evaluates up to eight forward and four substitution proposals on half of the offspring. Its runtime is 0.2188 s versus 0.0798 s for NSGA-II. Pareto Local Search is capped at 1600 neighbor evaluations, which matches the nominal offspring ceiling rather than the full BiLo-NSGA evaluation count.
issues.reviewer_inference: The reported hypervolume advantage does not isolate the project-level operators from additional search effort. Runtime disclosure is valuable, but it does not make the central quality comparison effort-matched, and the purportedly matched local-search control may receive substantially fewer candidate evaluations.
issues.required_action: Count every objective evaluation and local proposal evaluation. Recompare BiLo-NSGA, NSGA-II, and Pareto Local Search under an identical total-evaluation budget and, separately, an identical wall-clock budget on the same eight scenarios. The estimand is the per-run feasible-front hypervolume difference at matched effort; the analysis unit is one independent run, with 30 runs per method and a declared multiplicity family.
issues.acceptance_test: The revision reports evaluation-count distributions and matched-budget hypervolume tables for all eight scenarios, and scopes the headline advantage to whichever evaluation or runtime condition actually supports it.
issues.evidence_boundary: Without this control, the evidence licenses only a quality–computation trade-off for the disclosed implementations, not greater search efficiency or an operator-specific advantage at equal effort.

issues.location: Section 3.1 budget-violation equation; Section 4 formal definitions; Sections 4.2–4.5
issues.manuscript_evidence: Section 3.1 defines normalized violation as max(0,(cost-B)/B), whereas Section 4 redefines it in cost units as max(0,-s_B). The local fitness includes an unspecified penalty lambda. The insertion score uses undefined quantities b_jq and omega_q, while the prose alternates between equal weights and scenario-dependent scalar weights.
issues.reviewer_inference: These are behavior-changing ambiguities rather than cosmetic notation differences. The violation scale determines the penalty, and the undisclosed benefit components and weights determine every accepted insertion, substitution, and repair drop.
issues.required_action: Provide one consistent violation definition and state the implemented lambda, all per-scenario weight vectors, the definition and normalization of every b_jq term, tie-breaking rules, initialization distribution, offspring-local-search selection rule, and whether the local normalization equals the hypervolume normalization. Reconcile the equations, pseudocode, configuration files, and implementation.
issues.acceptance_test: A reader can reproduce every proposal ranking and acceptance decision from the manuscript and supplied configuration, and an implementation-conformance check shows that the equations and released code use the same units and parameter values.
issues.evidence_boundary: After closure, the paper may claim results for a precisely specified BiLo-NSGA configuration; the current text does not uniquely identify that configuration.

issues.manuscript_evidence: The paper motivates the method by dependency synergies and portfolio interactions, but the four optimization objectives are separable sums or a mean and contain no pairwise dependency benefit, prerequisite, or group constraint. Dependency information enters only through a fixed 1.06 proposal-ranking bonus. Disabling or thinning this mechanism produces no claimed resolved benefit.
issues.reviewer_inference: A search heuristic that favors an already represented group does not establish that the optimization problem models or captures dependency synergy. The current evidence supports budget coupling and a group-aware proposal bias, not optimization of inter-project dependency value.
issues.required_action: Either narrow all interaction and synergy claims to budget crowding and a heuristic group bonus, or define an operational dependency benefit or constraint in the problem and evaluate it. For the latter route, hold pool, budget, weights, and randomization fixed; compare the bonus and no-bonus controls over 30 runs, with dependency-value or dependency-constraint satisfaction and hypervolume as prespecified estimands.
issues.acceptance_test: Every dependency-related claim maps either to an explicit modeled quantity with a controlled result or is rewritten as a bounded description of proposal ordering without asserted synergy capture.
issues.evidence_boundary: The present experiment supports budget-aware portfolio search with a group-aware heuristic, not validated dependency-aware portfolio value.

issues.location: Introduction contribution 1; Sections 4.6, 6.6, and 7; Tables 4 and 7
issues.manuscript_evidence: The trace records accepted forward insertions, substitutions, and repair drops. Crossover, mutation, parentage, environmental selection, and portfolio lineage are not described as logged. Coverage means that a project appearing in the final front appeared in at least one logged operation somewhere in the run, and the manuscript reports about 3668 events per run.
issues.reviewer_inference: A run-level collection of local events does not necessarily provide the claimed account of the moves producing a particular final recommendation. Project-level coverage is not lineage coverage, replayability, semantic correctness, or review utility.
issues.required_action: Either rename the artifact as a run-level accepted-local-move log and remove recommendation-path language, or bind events to parent, offspring, generation, and final-solution identifiers while recording every unlogged state-changing operation. For the stronger claim, provide a replay test that reconstructs each returned portfolio exactly.
issues.acceptance_test: Either automated replay reconstructs 100% of final portfolios from their recorded lineages, or the manuscript consistently limits the claim to production and coverage of local-move records and makes no decision-path or explanation implication.
issues.evidence_boundary: Even after replay validation, the evidence would establish trace completeness, not explanation quality, human-review benefit, safety, or deployment readiness.

issues.manuscript_evidence: The proposed defaults include forward depth 8, substitution depth 4, local search on half the offspring, a 1.06 dependency bonus, scalarization weights, and a violation penalty. Apart from a combined shallow-depth ablation and disabling selected components, no controlled sensitivity is reported. The section called budget sensitivity changes scalar weights and random streams as well as budget.
issues.reviewer_inference: For a metaheuristic whose pooled margin over NSGA-II is 1.12% and whose operator effects reverse across settings, unexplored default sensitivity prevents assessment of application robustness and possible benchmark-specific tuning. The budget-indexed plot is correctly caveated but is not a budget-only sensitivity analysis.
issues.required_action: Disclose how defaults were chosen and whether the reported scenarios were visible during tuning. Run a prespecified sensitivity analysis for forward depth, substitution depth, local-search probability, dependency-bonus magnitude, and scalarization weights while holding the scenario, pool, budget, and randomization blocks fixed. Report mean hypervolume and runtime; the analysis unit is a run, with uncertainty across 30 runs.
issues.acceptance_test: The revision identifies parameter ranges over which the principal NSGA-II comparison and forward-versus-no-forward conclusion retain their direction, or explicitly limits the contribution to the single tested configuration.
issues.evidence_boundary: Closure licenses robustness only over the tested parameter ranges, not universal parameter insensitivity.

issues.location: Section 5.3 hypervolume normalization and reference-point specification
issues.manuscript_evidence: Per-experiment bounds are estimated from the empty portfolio, all singleton portfolios, and 2048 random feasible portfolios, after which every objective is clipped to [0,1]. No method-by-objective clipping frequency or reference-bound sensitivity is reported.
issues.reviewer_inference: An optimizer can exceed random-reference extrema, especially on benefit objectives. Clipping would collapse distinct high-quality portfolios onto the same boundary and could change small hypervolume contrasts, including the 1.12% headline difference.
issues.required_action: Report clipping counts and magnitudes for every method, scenario, and objective. Recompute the per-run hypervolumes using fixed, method-independent bounds demonstrated to contain all scored points and under at least one reasonable alternative reference point. The estimand is the BiLo-NSGA minus baseline hypervolume contrast; the analysis unit remains the run.
issues.acceptance_test: No scored point is silently clipped under the primary analysis, and the direction and inferential status of the headline comparisons are reported under the alternative normalization and reference-point choices.
issues.evidence_boundary: The primary hypervolume ranking is credible only for normalization choices under which it is shown to be stable.

issues.manuscript_evidence: NSGA-II and NSGA-III are described as constrained, while MOEA/D uses an unspecified budget penalty and returns no feasible portfolio in one reported panel. Reference-direction counts, MOEA/D decomposition and neighborhood settings, penalty magnitude, software versions, and infeasible-run rates are not reported.
issues.reviewer_inference: Different and incompletely specified feasibility handling can severely disadvantage MOEA/D and inflate the aggregate count of baseline wins. The very low MOEA/D hypervolume is not interpretable as algorithm-family inferiority without showing that its constraint treatment is viable.
issues.required_action: Disclose complete baseline configurations and feasibility rates. Re-run MOEA/D with comparable constraint handling or a documented penalty sensitivity/tuning protocol, and report the five-baseline win count both including and excluding any configuration that systematically fails to produce feasible fronts.
issues.acceptance_test: Every baseline has reproducible settings and a viable feasibility rate, or is explicitly labeled a failed configuration and removed from broad algorithm-family claims.
issues.evidence_boundary: The current evidence compares the disclosed implementations only and cannot support superiority over MOEA/D or Pareto local search as general method families.

issues.manuscript_evidence: The project_pool_scalability scenario retains the same 120-candidate full pool and changes the budget to 1.20 times nominal. The local_move_explainability and ranking_robustness scenarios also use the full pool and nominal budget, with their distinguishing manipulations not specified beyond possible scalar-weight changes.
issues.reviewer_inference: These labels suggest scalability, explanation, and robustness tests that the disclosed manipulations do not operationalize. The manuscript partly acknowledges this by calling one setting large-pool-labeled, but the labels still enter the mechanism narrative.
issues.required_action: Rename scenarios according to their actual controlled variables, disclose every weight or configuration difference, and remove scalability, robustness, or explainability implications unless a corresponding pool-size, perturbation, or human/trace-quality estimand is measured.
issues.acceptance_test: Each scenario name and result sentence identifies an observable manipulation, and no application property is inferred from a label alone.
issues.evidence_boundary: The existing cells support results for named benchmark configurations, not scalability, ranking robustness, or explanation quality.

issues.manuscript_evidence: Both sections contain explicit AUTHOR INPUT REQUIRED placeholders. CRediT roles, author approval, funding, grant information, and APC funding are not supplied.
issues.reviewer_inference: The submission is not publication-ready and these facts cannot be inferred by a reviewer or generated from the scientific content.
issues.required_action: Obtain confirmation from every author, insert verified CRediT roles, and provide the verified funding and APC statement or the journal's no-external-funding wording.
issues.acceptance_test: No declaration placeholder remains, all named authors have confirmed their roles, and the funding statement contains only human-verified information.
issues.evidence_boundary: No acceptance decision can be finalized while authorship and funding declarations remain unresolved.

issues.location: Contribution 2; Data Availability Statement; References 2 and 33
issues.manuscript_evidence: The text says the full generation code is released, while the Data Availability Statement says the package is available from the corresponding author and that a persistent archive can be supplied before publication. The package and companion TRACE-MOEA manuscript were not supplied here. Reference 2 contains a malformed DOI string with an extra closing brace inside the identifier.
issues.reviewer_inference: The benchmark, run archive, code, external-source contents, and companion-overlap assertions remain unverified within the supplied evidence. This is not by itself a demonstrated scientific defect, but the release-status contradiction and malformed reference require correction.
issues.required_action: Use one accurate availability statement, provide reviewers with the stated supplementary package and companion manuscript, deposit the final code/data/run records in a persistent accessible archive when redistribution permits, and correct the malformed DOI.
issues.acceptance_test: The stated package is accessible and contains the candidate generator, configurations, 4320 run records, inference tables, and backtest inputs; the availability wording matches the actual access state and all DOI links are syntactically valid.
issues.evidence_boundary: Until supplied, reproducibility and companion independence are manuscript assertions rather than independently verified findings.

issues.manuscript_evidence: The main text names real_project_review_inference_v2.csv, describes an original rectangular significance output retained as provenance, and notes that pre-atomic-substitution backtests remain suffixed and excluded.
issues.reviewer_inference: These version-history details support artifact governance but do not advance the scientific argument and draw attention to audit chronology in the main manuscript.
issues.required_action: Move filenames, superseded-output lineage, exclusion manifests, and version chronology to the supplement or repository documentation; retain only the final analysis definition and scientifically relevant exclusion rule in the article.
issues.acceptance_test: The main text describes the final protocol without internal version labels or incident-history language, while the supplementary archive preserves the complete provenance record.
issues.evidence_boundary: Artifact provenance can support reproducibility but does not strengthen the method-effect or application-validity claims.

claim_map.claim: BiLo-NSGA is a project-level, budget-aware local-search extension of NSGA-II.
claim_map.method_support: Forward insertion, atomic substitution, feasibility repair, dependency-biased proposal ranking, and non-dominated environmental selection are formally described.
claim_map.experiment_support: The full method is compared with NSGA-II and direct component controls across eight proxy scenarios.

claim_map.claim: BiLo-NSGA improves pooled hypervolume over NSGA-II by 1.12% on the eight-scenario benchmark.
claim_map.method_support: Both methods operate on the same stated objective definition and population/generation settings.
claim_map.experiment_support: Reported pooled means are 0.17190 and 0.17000, with scenario-level means, rank effects, and corrected tests.

claim_map.claim: BiLo-NSGA broadly outperforms five stochastic baselines.
claim_map.method_support: Five stochastic baseline implementations are included.
claim_map.experiment_support: The manuscript reports 37 positive mean differences and 36 corrected wins in 40 cells, with no significant loss.

claim_map.claim: Forward insertion has scenario-dependent positive effects rather than a universal pooled benefit.
claim_map.method_support: A no-forward control changes the forward component while retaining the remaining search framework.
claim_map.experiment_support: The full method wins significantly in three primary-family scenarios, while the no-forward control has the higher pooled mean and four scenarios remain unresolved.

claim_map.claim: Atomic substitution supplies replacement semantics but has no demonstrated hypervolume gain.
claim_map.method_support: The proposed move commits or rolls back removal and insertion atomically, and no-backward and legacy-deletion controls are present.
claim_map.experiment_support: Both controls have higher pooled means, and no scenario-level contrast involving substitution resolves significantly.

claim_map.claim: The method provides a reviewable decision path for returned recommendations.
claim_map.method_support: Accepted local moves and repairs are logged, but complete portfolio lineage through crossover, mutation, and selection is not established.
claim_map.experiment_support: The reported 99.6% statistic measures project occurrence in any logged event, not replayable recommendation-specific lineage or human utility.

claim_map.method_support: Dependency groups affect a 1.06 insertion-ranking bonus, but no dependency value or constraint appears in the optimization problem.
claim_map.experiment_support: No resolved dependency-bonus or dependency-density benefit is reported.

claim_map.claim: The NERC and MTEP16 analyses provide descriptive external consistency.
claim_map.method_support: Both backtests define explicit rule- or outcome-based readouts and disclose construct overlap and dependence limitations.
claim_map.experiment_support: NERC rank associations are nonsignificant; MTEP broad capture is 1.0715 while strict capture is near parity and underpowered.

claim_map.claim: The public proxy benchmark and full experimental archive are reproducible.
claim_map.method_support: Source families, pool size, archetypes, scenario structure, and deterministic-construction intent are described.
claim_map.experiment_support: The manuscript asserts availability of code, configurations, 4320 records, corrected inference tables, and figure scripts.

summary: Major revision is warranted. The manuscript is unusually candid about its modest gain, adverse pooled ablations, unresolved substitution effect, runtime cost, proxy scope, and descriptive backtests; those are substantial strengths. However, the headline comparison is not effort-matched, core equations and local-search weights do not uniquely specify the implementation, hypervolume clipping has not been audited, and the application-facing dependency and decision-path narratives exceed what the objective model and trace evidence establish. Baseline feasibility handling and parameter sensitivity also require correction. These defects are scientifically repairable through matched-budget controls, specification reconciliation, normalization and parameter sensitivity analyses, and claim narrowing. Author-contribution and funding placeholders are absolute pre-acceptance blockers, while external artifacts and bibliography contents remain unverified within the supplied evidence.
